newsitem.title: USA: Kentucky proposes $100 mln GOs for construction.
newsitem.headline: Kentucky proposes $100 mln GOs for construction.

text.p: FRANKFORT, Ky., May 6 (Retuer) - Kentucky Budget Director Jim Ramsey has recommended the state issue $100 million general obligation bonds to finance 27 construction projects approved in last year's legislative session, the Herald-Leader reported Tuesday.

The projects were originally to be funded from a cash surplus. Gov. Paul Patton has recommended that the surplus money be used instead to pay for education projects and to partly fund $214 million court-ordered intangibles tax refunds.
Ramsey briefed the legislature's education committee Monday on issues they are likely to face in a special legislative session that begins next week.

Ramsey also said that although long-range forecasts had projected a $13 million budget shortfall by fiscal 1999, state economists are now confident economic growth will eliminate the threat of a deficit.
He noted that during the last four budget years, Kentucky's actual revenues have outpaced initial estimates by $48 million to $178 million a year.
